notes: Median/average annual BASE salary benchmarks by Crustdata role family x location tier. US cells: BLS OEWS May 2025 medians (government, all employers & experience levels; SF tier = San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont MSA, San Jose MSA value attached where available). London: ONS ASHE 2025 revised, Table 15 (work region London, full-time, SOC2020 4-digit), weekly basic pay median x 52.143. India, Toronto, Singapore, Berlin and all Product Management cells: Payscale self-reported AVERAGE base salary (city pages); Payscale skews lower than BLS for the same metro, so cross-source comparisons carry roughly +/-15% noise. Founders: Kruze Consulting (US) and Creandum/Sifted (Europe). Role->occupation mappings are proxies where no exact code exists (noted per cell in 'occupation'/'method_note'). FX: ECB euro reference rates of 2026-10-30, cross-converted to USD. Fill missing cells with location_index x the 'Other US' (BLS national) role median, then apply employer_tiers multipliers. Not sourced/left null: Bangalore founders; Remote/Other tier; Paris/Amsterdam. Seniority is not controlled anywhere: these are all-level medians.

switch_premium.notes: US realised pay change for job-changers (ADP Pay Insights, Sept 2026 report): base pay +4.8% YoY vs +3.0% for job-stayers; gross pay +7.3% vs +4.4%. So the US switch PREMIUM over staying is only ~1.8-2.9 percentage points; changers' total raise is ~5-7%. Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker (Jan 2026): switchers 4.7% vs stayers 3.5%. India is different: foundit Appraisal Survey (June 2026, n>2,500) found 70% of professionals expect >=21% to switch, modal bracket 21-30% (27% of respondents), vs Aon's projected 2026 appraisal raise of 9.1% (8.9% actual in 2025). These Indian figures are EXPECTATIONS, not realised raises; no reputable 2025-26 source on realised India switch hikes was found. Verdict on the 20-25% hypothesis: plausible as an India/tech expectation; far too high as a US average (US realised ~5-7%).
